c.tagline: Pacific port city famed for cruise ships, Valle de Guadalupe wine country, and fresh seafood.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis do not use meters; agree on the fare with the driver before starting the ride, especially for airport or Valle de Guadalupe trips.

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's national emergency number, connecting to police, fire, and medical services.

avoid.reason: Tourist zone safe; caution in outer areas (Baja cartel presence)

hood_desc: The historic waterfront core along Boulevard Costero and Avenida López Mateos, home to the cruise terminal, the Riviera del Pacífico cultural center, and the fish market; best for first-timers who want fish tacos, souvenir shops, and cantinas all within walking distance.

The stretch of coastal hotels and restaurants south of downtown along Boulevard Costero, popular with cruise passengers and weekend visitors from California; suits travelers who want an oceanfront base close to the action without staying right downtown.

A hillside residential area above downtown known for its lookout point over the bay and marina, with a handful of boutique hotels and restaurants; good for those wanting quiet and a view over the noise of the port.

Mexico's premier wine region, about 30-40 minutes northeast of the city, dotted with boutique wineries, farm-to-table restaurants, and design-forward small hotels; suits travelers prioritizing wine tastings and countryside scenery over city sights.
A quieter stretch of sand and lagoon south of the city with family-oriented resorts and water sports; suits families and travelers wanting a beach base away from the cruise crowds.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water, as everywhere in Mexico.

transit.hours: Buses generally run about 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; no night service, so taxis or ride apps cover late hours.
transit.pay: Cash paid to the driver on board (roughly 10-12 pesos per ride); there is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.note: Ensenada has no metro or rail transit; local 'camiones urbanos' (urban buses) and taxis are the main public transport, with ride-hailing apps also available downtown.

bus: ABC (Autotransportes de Baja California) intercity buses to Tijuana, Mexicali, and Tecate

transit.m: ABC intercity bus toward Ensenada (transfer required)

tip.r: 10-15% at sit-down restaurants is standard and expected; not usually added automatically except for large groups.
